why_how.text: Use headlights whenever seeing other road users becomes difficult, so they can see your vehicle too.

Turn the headlights on as daylight begins to fade.
When driving requires lights, use headlights rather than parking lights.

Use the horn when it can help prevent a collision.
Without immediate danger, use a light horn tap rather than a sharp blast.

Use a light horn tap if a driver starts moving into your lane as you pass.

Speed up or fall back from another vehicle’s blind spot so its driver can see you more easily.
When passing, move through the other driver’s blind spot as promptly as possible.

Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react.
